Yes, aripiprazole has been associated with an increased risk of pathological gambling in some patients. Aripiprazole, also known by its brand name Abilify, is an atypical antipsychotic medication used to treat various mental health conditions, including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder. 

There have been reports and studies suggesting that aripiprazole may contribute to the development of impulse control disorders, including pathological gambling, in a small subset of patients. This is thought to be related to the medication's effect on dopamine receptors in the brain, which can influence impulse control and reward processing.

As a result, regulatory agencies such as the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) have added warnings to the labeling of aripiprazole regarding the potential risk of pathological gambling and other impulse control disorders. Patients taking aripiprazole should be monitored for signs of these disorders and report any concerns to their healthcare provider.
